title: Nil identity must be guarded in auth hooks before dereference
answers: Panic in ClearUserPermissionCacheHook on nil identity
Login fails with confusing nil pointer dereference instead of real auth error
Why does a secondary panic mask the original authentication failure
Guard pattern for identity.Requester possibly nil in sync hooks
body:
Symptom: a failed login flow triggers a nil pointer panic inside ClearUserPermissionCacheHook, which masks the original authentication error that caused ident to be nil.
Root cause: pkg/services/authn/authnimpl/sync/rbac_sync.go:ClearUserPermissionCacheHook only checked `err != nil` before using `ident`, but hooks can be invoked with a nil identity even when err is nil (or ident can be nil independent of err).
Fix pattern: add an explicit nil check for the identity/requester parameter alongside the error check (`if err != nil || ident == nil { return }`) before any dereference, in any hook that receives an identity.Requester that may legitimately be nil on auth failure paths.
Constraints: applies to post-login/auth hooks that accept a possibly-nil identity.Requester; does not apply where the caller guarantees non-nil identity by contract.
applies: authn hooks in pkg/services/authn/authnimpl/sync that receive identity.Requester and run after login/auth events

The root cause is that ClearUserPermissionCacheHook in pkg/services/authn/authnimpl/sync/rbac_sync.go checked only `err != nil` but hooks can receive nil identity even when err is nil, causing nil pointer panics that mask the original authentication error. Fix by adding `if err != nil || ident == nil { return }` before any dereference of the identity parameter. This applies to post-login/auth hooks in pkg/services/authn/authnimpl/sync that accept possibly-nil identity.Requester, but does not apply where the caller's contract guarantees non-nil identity.
